 Almost 14,000 BMW vehicles recalled due to fire risk
 BMW Australia has issued its sixth fire-risk recall this year, advising owners of 13,696 cars to park outdoors away from buildings and other vehicles.
 6 hours ago    Comments Damion Smy 
 Deputy News Editor
 Show all photos Damion Smy 
 Deputy News Editor
 BMW Australia is recalling 13,696 vehicles due to an electrical issue that could cause a fire. Owners are advised to park outdoors away from buildings and other vehicles until rectification work is carried out.
 The recall covers vehicles built between 2011 and 2018, including the BMW 2 Series (228i), 3 Series (325i and 328i), 4 Series (428i), 5 Series (520i and 528i), X1 , X3 and X5 . It also affects 191 examples of the E89 BMW Z4 sports car.
 “An improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump may become exposed to moisture over time and short circuit. A short circuit increases the risk of a vehicle fire, smoke or a burning smell whilst driving or when exiting the vehicle,” says the official recall notice.
 “A vehicle fire could increase the risk of injury or death to vehicle occupants, other road users, bystanders and/or damage to property.”

 “As a precaution, vehicles should be parked outdoors away from structures and other vehicles until the recall has been completed,” the recall notice advised.
 “Once a remedy becomes available, BMW will contact affected owners to schedule an appointment for inspection. If required, repairs will be carried out, free of charge.”
 The latest recall follows two fire-risk recalls issued by BMW Australia in July 2026 .
 One of those recalls affected 10,559 vehicles built between 2020 and 2025 due to a starter motor issue that could cause overheating and lead to a fire.
 That recall affected the BMW 2 Series, 3 Series, 4 Series and 5 Series, as well as the X3 and X4 SUVs and the G29 Z4 sports car.
 BMW also recalled 16,578 vehicles built between 2020 and 2023 over a fire risk in February 2026 . That recall covered the 2 Series, 3 Series, 4 Series, 5 Series and 7 Series , as well as the X3, X4, X5 and G29 Z4.
 Owners of affected vehicles can contact their nearest authorised BMW dealer for further details.
 They can also contact BMW Australia by calling 1800 243 675, emailing info@bmw.com.au or visiting the BMW Australia recall portal .
